item.title: China vows to foster stable environment for business cooperation with Australia: premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 20 -- China stands ready to work with Australia to eliminate disruptions to normal economic and trade exchanges, and provide a favorable environment and stable expectations for business cooperation between the two countries, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Friday. Li made the remarks while jointly attending the 9th China-Australia CEO Roundtable with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Beijing. Li said China-Australia relations and cooperation have made considerable new progress over the past year under the strategic guidance of the leaders of the two countries. These hard-won achievements came amid severe disruptions to international trade and sluggish global economic growth, fully demonstrating the strong inherent momentum of bilateral cooperation, he said. Practice has repeatedly shown that China and Australia have highly complementary economic strengths and extensive common interests, making them natural partners for cooperation and opportunities for each other's development, Li added. Noting that global development still faces many uncertainties, Li said that stable and reliable partners are all the more important in times of uncertainty. China and Australia should further strengthen economic and trade ties to achieve broader and higher-level mutually beneficial cooperation, he said. Li called on the two sides to deepen cooperation in three key areas. First, the two countries should focus on consumption upgrading to improve people's quality of life. While consolidating and expanding traditional trade in agricultural and food products, they should tap the potential for cooperation in tourism, education, healthcare and elderly care, biomedicine and high-end medical services, and develop more high-quality products and services to meet people's needs throughout their lives. Second, the two sides should strengthen innovation cooperation, particularly in digital and intelligent technologies. They should better integrate their respective strengths in innovation, enhance mutual empowerment and deepen cooperation in the application and industrialization of new technologies, so as to accelerate the transformation of research achievements into new products and orders for businesses in both countries and better share the benefits of innovation. Third, the two countries should deepen cooperation in green and low-carbon transition for sustainable development. They should jointly develop competitive green products, build green steel supply chains and new energy vehicle industrial and supply chains, explore third-party markets together, and move up the global green value chain. Li stressed that the Chinese government stands ready to work with the Australian government to keep bilateral relations on the right direction, maintain win-win cooperation as the prevailing trend, and eliminate disruptions to normal economic and trade exchanges, so as to provide a favorable environment and stable expectations for business cooperation. China's door to the outside world will only open wider, and more Australian companies are welcome to deepen their presence in the Chinese market, Li said. He expressed hope that the business communities of both countries would continue to serve as pioneers of mutually beneficial cooperation and promoters of bilateral friendship, and help achieve new results in China-Australia economic and trade cooperation. Albanese said China is Australia's largest trading partner, and that bilateral economic and trade cooperation contributes to the economic development of both countries and brings tangible benefits to their peoples. Noting that next year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Australia and China, Albanese said Australia stands ready to take this opportunity to strengthen mutually beneficial cooperation with China in areas such as artificial intelligence, green transition and modern agriculture, and deepen people-to-people and cultural exchanges. He expressed hope that the business communities of the two countries would learn from each other, draw on each other's experiences, expand cooperation, and make greater contributions to the development of Australia-China relations.

item.title: China ready to accelerate FTA upgrade talks with Singapore: premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 21 -- China stands ready to work with Singapore to accelerate negotiations on the China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (FTA) 4.0 and promote a higher level of two-way opening-up, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said Saturday. Li made the remarks during talks with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Beijing. Li said China is willing to strengthen strategic communication with Singapore, consolidate political mutual trust, support each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns, and expand practical cooperation. The two sides should strive for more achievements in their all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership and continuously improve the well-being of the two peoples, Li said. Li called on the two sides to further strengthen industrial integration, upgrade major bilateral government-to-government cooperation projects, and deepen cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence, clean energy, connectivity and finance. The two countries should also advance the development of the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor to inject fresh impetus into their development, he said. Noting that China and Singapore share similar approaches to social governance and face many common challenges, Li called for greater exchanges and mutual learning to address population aging, promote balanced development and improve public services. The two sides should also expand people-to-people and cultural cooperation in areas such as tourism, culture and youth exchanges, he added. Li said China and Singapore should forge closer coordination and cooperation within the United Nations, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) and other relevant frameworks, firmly promote regional economic integration, advance the building of an open world economy, uphold the multilateral trading system and safeguard their common interests. China supports Singapore in assuming the rotating chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) next year, and stands ready to work with Singapore to encourage all parties to implement the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol effectively, Li said. Wong congratulated China on successfully hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen. He said Singapore and China have built a strong partnership based on deep mutual trust over the past decades. Singapore looks forward to maintaining closer high-level exchanges with China, strengthening the alignment of development strategies, deepening cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence, the digital economy, green energy and connectivity, and enhancing people-to-people and cultural exchanges, Wong said. Singapore stands ready to work with China to achieve more results in their all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership, he added. Wong said Singapore supports the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity and the four global initiatives proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, and appreciates China's leadership in maintaining world peace and promoting openness and development.

item.title: Chinese vice premier to visit Singapore
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
BEIJING, Nov. 20 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang will visit Singapore from November 22 to 23 at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister of Singapore Gan Kim Yong, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Friday. Ding, member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, will co-chair with Gan bilateral cooperation mechanism meetings, the spokesperson said. The meetings include the 22nd meeting of the China-Singapore Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation, the 27th meeting of the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park Joint Steering Council, the 18th meeting of the China-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City Joint Steering Council, and the 10th meeting of the China-Singapore (Chongqing) Demonstration Initiative on Strategic Connectivity Joint Steering Council, according to the spokesperson.

item.title: China, Australia should focus on common interests, expand cooperation in green development, AI: Chinese premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
BEIJING, Nov. 20 -- China is willing to work with Australia to focus on common interests and boost cooperation in areas including green development and artificial intelligence (AI), Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Friday. Li made the remarks during the 11th China-Australia Annual Leaders' Meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Beijing. Noting next year marks the 55th anniversary of China-Australia diplomatic relations, Li said China stands ready to work with Australia to seize this opportunity to focus on common interests, properly manage differences, and deliver more outcomes in the comprehensive strategic partnership. China is willing to expand trade volume and optimize its structure with Australia, develop cooperation highlights in emerging areas such as green and low-carbon development, new energy vehicles and AI, and further enhance trade and investment liberalization and facilitation, Li said. The two sides should make next year's China-Australia Year of Tourism a success and deepen exchanges and cooperation in culture, youth, local areas, media and think tanks, the premier noted. China will strengthen communication and coordination with Australia within the UN, APEC and other frameworks, jointly uphold the multilateral system and free trade, and safeguard international fairness and justice, he said. Albanese congratulated China on successfully hosting the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in south China. He said Australia and China should take a long-term perspective, not let differences disrupt bilateral relations, and actively advance cooperation. Albanese said Australia is willing to deepen cooperation with China in economy and trade, agriculture, energy and other fields, and accelerate cooperation in emerging fields like clean energy, AI, electric vehicles and digital economy. Full text: Statement on Joint Outcomes of the China-Australia Annual Leaders' Meeting

item.title: Xi, Prabowo announce launch of China-Indonesia comprehensive economic partnership negotiations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Friday announced the launch of negotiations for a bilateral comprehensive economic partnership. The announcement was made during Xi's meeting with Prabowo in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Prabowo is in China for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. Xi said the two countries should strengthen strategic communication and solidarity, deepen all-round strategic cooperation, consolidate the foundation of political trust, and jointly guard against and respond to external risks. He called on both countries to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, advance major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, and deepen cooperation in energy and mineral resources, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, and clean energy. Xi called for efforts to reach an all-round, high-standard comprehensive economic partnership agreement at an early date. Amid emerging risks and challenges in the world, China is ready to strengthen coordination and cooperation with Indonesia within multilateral frameworks, including the United Nations, APEC and China-ASEAN cooperation, Xi said. Prabowo said Indonesia's strategic partnership with China is stronger than ever, reaffirming that Indonesia firmly adheres to the one-China policy and that Taiwan is a province of the People's Republic of China. Indonesia sincerely welcomes Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in the country, and is committed to providing a reliable, stable and predictable business environment, Prabowo said. Prabowo said Indonesia highly appreciates China's role as a responsible major country in international affairs, and stands ready to work with China to safeguard the shared interests of the Global South and promote regional and global peace and stability.

item.title: Xi says China, Singapore should strengthen strategic communication, enhance coordination
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Friday that China and Singapore should strengthen strategic communication and enhance solidarity and coordination as the world is undergoing accelerated changes unseen in a century. The two countries should be sincere friends who trust each other and support each other in pursuing development paths suited to their respective national conditions, said Xi when meeting with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Wong attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen. During the meeting, Xi called for advancing the all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership between China and Singapore to new heights, and stressed the need for both sides to advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. The two countries should launch negotiations for upgraded Version 4.0 of their free trade agreement, and deliver signature cooperation outcomes in areas such as the digital economy, green development, and artificial intelligence, Xi added. Noting that both countries should be "a progressive force" for championing international fairness and justice, Xi called for safeguarding regional peace and stability while jointly building an Asia-Pacific community and a community with a shared future for humanity. For his part, Wong stated that Singapore firmly adheres to the one-China policy and opposes "Taiwan independence." Singapore stands ready to work with China to enhance political mutual trust, deepen cooperation in areas such as trade, industrial and supply chains, and artificial intelligence, and promote people-to-people exchanges, the prime minister noted. Wong said Singapore is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the Chinese side on international affairs to jointly address global challenges.

item.title: Xi calls for promoting building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to higher level
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday called for promoting the building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to a higher level. China and Thailand should continuously enhance political mutual trust and strengthen solidarity and coordination, Xi said when meeting with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The two countries should step up exchanges between governments, political parties, legislatures and at other levels, and safeguard their common strategic interests, Xi stressed. He called on the two sides to make good use of cooperation mechanisms in economy and trade, science and technology, and the digital economy, expand and strengthen traditional cooperation in agriculture and connectivity, and cultivate and strengthen new growth areas of cooperation such as artificial intelligence, new energy vehicles, aviation and aerospace, disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, and water resources management. The two sides should strengthen cooperation in culture, education, and tourism, Xi added. He also urged intensifying efforts to crack down on illegal and criminal activities such as online gambling and telecom fraud. The two sides should strengthen multilateral coordination and work together to safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xi said. China is ready to play a positive role in bringing about an early turnaround in Thailand-Cambodia relations, Xi said. For his part, Anutin said Thailand is ready to continue to strengthen high-level exchanges with China and enhance cooperation in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, industrial and supply chains, and connectivity. Thailand will resolutely crack down on cross-border crimes including online gambling and telecom fraud, and protect the safety of Chinese citizens in Thailand, he said, adding that the country welcomes more Chinese visitors. Anutin attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, held from Wednesday to Thursday.

item.title: Xi says China ready for closer cooperation with Malaysia
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 -- China stands ready to foster greater momentum for cooperation with Malaysia to bring more benefits to people of both countries, President Xi Jinping said Friday. China-Malaysia relations have maintained high-level development since the two sides reached important consensus on building a high-level strategic China-Malaysia community with a shared future and ushered in a new "Golden 50 Years" for bilateral ties in April last year, he said. Xi made the remarks when meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. China and Malaysia should maintain high-level strategic communication and support each other in safeguarding their respective national sovereignty, security and development interests, Xi said at the meeting. The two sides should also ensure high-quality development and operation of key projects, expand and improve agricultural product trade, and broaden cooperation in tourism, education and other areas, he added. Xi called for joint efforts to advance the reform of global governance, strengthen coordination and cooperation within multilateral frameworks such as APEC, and safeguard the common interests of developing countries. Anwar said the Taiwan question is China's internal affair, and Malaysia firmly adheres to the one-China policy. He said Malaysia is ready to strengthen strategic coordination with China, give full play to the role of bilateral cooperation mechanisms, ensure the sound operation of key infrastructure projects, and enhance cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence. Malaysia will also promote inter-civilization exchanges and dialogue, step up coordination and collaboration in international affairs, and keep elevating the level of Malaysia-China relations, Anwar said. Anwar attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen.

item.title: Xi says China, Australia should be mutually trusted partners
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Friday that China and Australia should be cooperative partners who trust each other and help each other succeed, as the two countries have no historical grievances or conflicts of fundamental interests. China-Australia relations are stable at present, said Xi when meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Albanese is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. As next year marks the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Australia, Xi called on the two sides to achieve greater progress in bilateral relations from a new starting point. Xi said that in a volatile and turbulent world, the two countries should enhance mutual trust, accommodate each other's core interests and major concerns, and keep to the right direction of friendship and cooperation. He called for deepening mutually beneficial cooperation in pursuit of the two countries' respective development goals, advancing traditional cooperation in agriculture, energy and minerals, and expanding cooperation in emerging areas such as the green economy, new energy, the digital industry, artificial intelligence (AI) and climate change response. Efforts should be made to promote friendship between the two countries through expanded people-to-people exchanges, Xi said, noting that the two sides had agreed to designate 2027 as the China-Australia Year of Tourism. He also emphasized the need to strengthen multilateral coordination in addressing global challenges, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community, and jointly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order based on international law. Albanese said that the improvement and development of Australia-China relations serves the interests of both sides and brings tangible benefits to the peoples of both countries. He said that Australia stands ready to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen practical cooperation in trade, investment, AI and other areas, deepen people-to-people exchanges, respect each other and properly handle differences, so as to make Australia-China relations an example for countries with different systems to develop constructive relations.
